To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the productivity levels of the nations of our sample have not converged; (ii) there is little evidence that the forces of convergence have been strong enough to counterbalance the forces of divergence; (iii) there is some evidence that the forces making for convergence may have become stronger since 1950; (iv) the forces making for divergence have not become weaker; and (v) the forces of convergence and divergence have been counterbalanced so that the growth rates of nations in our sample
the forces that have made for convergence are counterbalanced by forces that have made nations grow at rates that depend on initial income.
